pages.title: Coup de Grace
pages.content:
{{rune header|Coup de Grace}}

== Notes ==
* '''Coup de Grace''' only triggers on damage dealt after the champion is brought {{as|below 40% health}}.

== Trivia ==
* '''Coup de Grace''' is a French {{w|Coup de grâce|phrase}} that literally translates to "stroke of grace" or "blow of mercy", a final strike on one that is mortally wounded. It effectively means "knockout", "lethal blow", "killing stroke" or "deathblow".
* '''Coup de Grace''' behaves similarly to the removed Season 2016 mastery {{mi6|Merciless}}.

== Patch History ==
{{Scroll box|content=
;[[V25.S1.3]]
* Now affects {{sti|true damage}} dealt, excluding {{si|Smite}}.

;[[V9.8]]
* Bonus damage increased to 8% from 7%.
* {{sbc|Removed:}} No longer grants {{adaptive|15}} for 10 seconds upon scoring a champion {{tip|takedown}}.

;[[V8.2]]
* Damage amplifier reduced to 7% from 9%.

;[[V7.24]]
* Damage amplifier reduced to 9% from 10%.

;[[V7.22]] Added
* [[File:Precision icon.png|20px|link=Precision]] [[Precision]] Slot 3 rune.
** {{sbc|Passive:}} Deal 10% increased damage to champions {{as|below 40% health}}.
** Additionally, you gain {{as|9 '''bonus''' Attack Damage}} or {{as|15 Ability Power}} (Adaptive) for 10 seconds whenever you score a champion takedown. This bonus does not stack.
** {{sbc|Adaptive:}} Grants bonuses based on which stat you already have the most bonuses for. ''Defaults to the first listed.''
}}

{{Rune footer}}

pages.title: Damage
pages.content:
{{ToDo|This article and the '''Damage types''' section in particular contain confusing or outdated information that is presently subject to a complete overhaul.}} : {{hatnote|''Not to be confused with [[attack damage]], a champion statistic, nor conflated with [[Health#Health as a casting resource|health costs]], which are not damage.''}} [[File:Damage Annie.png|thumb|200px|Damage is displayed as a red section on a champion's health bar.]] '''Damage''' is the result of a direct [[combat]] interaction between two units: a source [[unit]] causes a deduction of a target unit's current [[health]] via a ''damaging'' [[spell]] (or accompanying [[debuff]]). Damage takes place in [[Tick and updates|engine time]] ("instantaneously") and the application itself is formally called a '''damage instance''' or '''damage event'''. {{tip|Invulnerability}} prevents damage, and {{tip|shield|shields}} can protect from it. Damage values can also be modified by the source or the target through [[damage modifier]]s. They can also be increased by a percentage due to an event called a {{tip|critical strike}}. Enemies are [[kill|slain]] upon dealing enough '''damage''' to deplete their [[health]]. A champion dealing damage against another champion triggers kill attribution (if it does not slay them otherwise) and, if the damage-dealer is within enemy {{tip|turret}} attack range, also triggers the turret's aggression until they exit the turret's range. == Types == The following three '''damage types''' exist: {{as|{{sbc|Physical}}|physical damage}}, {{as|{{sbc|Magic}}|magic damage}}, and {{as|{{sbc|True}}|true damage}}. Each damage event can fall under only one of these three categories. These three types exist to add variability to gameplay beyond simple deduction of health equal to the source's outgoing damage value, by potentially reducing, or '''''mitigating''''' it instead. * {{as|Physical damage}} is innately mitigated by {{stil|armor}}, a statistic that units possess. * {{as|Magic damage}} is innately mitigated by {{stil|magic resistance}}, a statistic that units possess. * {{as|True damage}} cannot be mitigated by any innate statistic. Aside from these innate mitigations, various effects can also reduce outgoing damage by a source (e.g. {{si|Exhaust}}), reduce incoming damage from all or some sources (e.g. {{cai|Meditate|Master Yi}}), potentially nullify any damage received (e.g. {{tip|invulnerability}}) or prevent an effect, which may or may not be accompanied by damage, from being applied altogether (e.g. {{tip|spell shield}}). {{as|True damage}} additionally has the property of being largely unaffected by damage ''reductions'', with the exception of {{cai|Riposte|Fiora}}, which invariably reduces all incoming non-{{tip|execute|execution}} damage dealt by sources other than {{tip|turrets}} by 100%. Effects that trigger from damage '''type''' will always occur, unless prevented from applying altogether, regardless of its classification. == Additional classification == In addition to types, damage instances can have multiple other classifications to determine and manage interactions systemically. Note that damage instances can equal zero (i.e. a health deduction, of zero). This is most commonly utilized for triggering [[kill]] attribution and minion aggression. === Tags === The '''tag''' system is a restrictive classification applicable to the ''source'' of the damage instance. It is restrictive because each tag entails a number of default ''properties'' the damage instance can have, and spells that interact with other spells can choose to ignore certain tags. Damage instances can have any combination of these '''tags''', though some combinations are atypical or never found in game. Properties are a secondary classification system, explained further below. * '''BasicAttack:'''The {{SITENAME}} elected to call this 'basic damage' and avoid using the term 'attack' in order to prevent confusion between the damage type, the action, and the [[attack damage]] statistic. Represents the base damage of all champion [[basic attack]]s (invariably), most empowered attacks (e.g. {{cai|Power Fist|Blitzcrank}}, {{cai|Crippling Strike|Darius}}), most attack-like abilities/also referred to as attack-spells (e.g. {{cai|Mystic Shot|Ezreal}}, {{cai|Lunge|Fiora}}) and all attack modifiers (e.g. {{cai|Heroic Swing|Akshan}}, {{cai|Royal Maelstrom|Bel'Veth}}, {{cai|Purge|Urgot}}, {{iis|Runaan's Hurricane}} {{nie|Wind's Fury}} bolts). ** All champion basic attacks, which are tagged with this, apply {{stil|life steal}} and {{tip|on-hit|on-hit effects}} through the ApplyLifesteal and TriggerOnHitEvents properties, respectively, as a fundamental mechanic. However other damage tags can have these properties, meaning they are not exclusive to this tag. * '''ActiveSpell:''' Represents most [[active]] [[champion ability|champion]] and [[active ability items|item abilities]], i.e., ones that the player has issued an active command, and paid a cost if applicable, to cast. ** This tag allows triggering {{tip|ability effects}} (invariably). * '''AOE:''' Represents damage in an area ('''A'''rea '''o'''f '''E'''ffect) or sometimes across multiple units. ** This tag is usually tied to penalties compared to other damage tags, since area effects are considered easier to apply than single-target effects. * '''Periodic:''' Represents effects repeating at a cadence generally shorter than traditional [[cooldown]]s and over a period, instead of at once. The repetition can originate from a continually firing spell (e.g. {{cai|The Culling|Lucian}}, {{cai|Tormented Shadow|Morgana}}) or be applied via a debuff (e.g. {{cai|Malefic Visions|Malzahar}}, {{cai|Poison Trail|Singed}}, {{iis|Liandry's Torment}} {{nie|Torment}}). ** This tag is usually tied to even stricter penalties compared to AOE and additionally has the property of not expunging {{tip|sleep}}. * '''Proc:'''The term 'proc' refers to a mechanic that has a chance of triggering, which is common in games such as World of Warcraft (e.g., "Your attacks have an x % chance to cause [...]" effects). League of Legends originally featured 'true' proc effects (e.g., "your attacks have a chance to slow.") However, the design philosophy of Riot Games' over-time grew more towards preferring 'on-hit' or "every nth attack" to purely random mechanics. Despite this: the engine-level label persisted. The term 'proc' now describes all additional effect triggers even if they are not guaranteed, 'proc' is used as a verb when triggering such an effect. Represents all effects applied as secondary on top of other more interactive effects. This is used for any damage that should not trigger a chain of additional [[attack effects|attack]] and [[spell effects|spell effects]] due to other damage tags on a target. {{tip|On-hit}} and {{tip|spell effects}} themselves are usually tagged proc. ** This tag is self-limiting; it exists so that effects that trigger from other damage tags do not continuously apply and/or repeat. * '''Indirect:''' Represents effects that are to be considered "not actively or directly sourced by the player themselves". ** In addition to not expunging {{tip|sleep}} like Periodic, and being self-limiting like Proc, this tag is reserved for use in other systems that require exclusion of all other damage types. It is rare and any further uses as of [[2026 Annual Cycle|2026]] are {{tt|unknown|This used to interact with pre-rework Neeko disguise.}}. * '''Pet:''' Represents all damage originating from [[champion summoned units]], also to defer attribution to their summoner. * '''Item:''' Represents damage originating from most non-champion spells. Despite the name, this includes [[summoner spell]] damage against champions, in addition to [[item]] abilities. ** This tag is generally exclusionary; it exists so that non-champion-sourced damage is identified and grouped separately from other champion-sourced damage, as a lesser category, and so that it does not remain untagged, for consistency. Damage instances which are supposed to remain unaffected by effects that modify champion attacks or ability damage are also tagged as such. * '''NonRedirectable:''' Represents all damage that manipulates the source of the instance. It has no current known applications, except (presumably) {{cais|Sleepy Trouble Bubble|Zoe}} expunging of {{tip|sleep}} specifically. It may be vestigial. * '''DoesNotAggroJungle:''' Represents all damage that should not trigger neutral {{tip|monster}} aggression, which includes {{cai|Friend of the Forest|Ivern}} and the regular damage of {{ii|Gustwalker Hatchling|icononly=true}}{{ii|Mosstomper Seedling|icononly=true}}{{ii|Scorchclaw Pup|icononly=true}} [[jungle]] companions. * '''OnHit:''' Represents all {{tip|on-hit|on-hit effects}} (invariably). ** This tag exists for interaction with effects that modify and/or repeat on-hit effect application. * '''Augment:''' Represents damage dealt by [[augment]] systems in modes such as {{tip|Arena}} and {{tip|ARAM: Mayhem}} (invariably). ** This tag exists for interaction with effects that modify and/or repeat augment effect application. The same origin spell can have any number of damage instances, even occurring simultaneously. It can also apply different damage instances with different tags depending on the target, or even the number of targets hit (the latter includes effects such as {{cai|Lay Waste|Karthus}}). In addition to all of the above, damage can be made to ignore {{tip|shield|shields}} and other forms of health manipulation internally. This is not handled by any known tags or properties. It is however most relevant for damage that does not fall under any tag. === Untagged === Untagged damaging effects also exist, which can have completely custom properties, though they are rare. On the {{SITENAME}}, these are referred to as {{tip|default damage}} (not official terminology). Some examples are listed below. * All {{tip|execute|executes}} ({{bi|Aspect of the Dragon|Elder Immolation}}, {{cai|Death from Below|Pyke}}, {{cai|Satchel Charge|Ziggs}} against {{tip|turrets}}, etc), which ignore shields. * The [[Nexus Obelisk]]'s damage, which ignores shields. * {{cais|Crescendum|Aphelios}} attack secondary damage. * {{cai|Fired Up!|Milio}} when applied via self-cast only. * {{iis|Umbral Glaive}} {{nie|Blackout}} ward damage. * A portion of all zero-damage instance spells, such as {{cai|Tempered Fate|Bard}}, {{cais|Time Bomb|Zilean}} application, {{cais|Pillar of Ice|Trundle}} displacement, and {{sis|Ignite}} application (exists separately to its ticks of non-zero damage). Untagged effects which ''also'' bypass death protection are termed {{tip|raw damage}}. In the context of champions, this only includes the Nexus Obelisk's damage against them specifically (it uniquely respects death protection against non-champions) and {{cais|Cell Division|Zac}} damage redirection. It is however common in other systems, such as the pit {{uis|Rift Herald}} Eye damage, the summoned {{uis|Rift Herald|Mercenary}} self-damage when hitting a turret, {{uis|Scryer's Bloom|Mutated Scryer's Bloom}} {{tip|ward}} damage in the [[Chemtech Rift]], and others. === Properties === Damage '''properties''' determine the ''behavior'' of the damage instance. As stated above, tags can imply certain properties as implemented, but apart from ActiveSpell's behavior these are technically {{tt|completely customizable|This can lead to certain unique or unexpected interactions.}}. * '''ApplyAttackRatio:''' (Unknown) * '''ApplyCritical:''' (Unknown) * '''ApplyDamageModifier:''' When disabled, the damage instance will be unaffected by damage modifiers. * '''ApplyLifesteal:''' When enabled, the damage instance applies {{stil|life steal}}. Unlike {{tip|vamp}} effects, this is not {{tip|healing}} through damage dealt. Healing modifiers that affect {{sti|life steal}} also affect spells with this tag. * '''ApplyOmnivamp:''' When enabled, the damage instance applies {{stil|omnivamp}}. * '''ApplyPhysicalVamp:''' When enabled, the damage instance applies {{stil|physical vamp}}. Due to the stat being unused, this property is likewise deprecated. * '''ApplySpellvamp:''' When enabled, the damage instance applies {{stil|spell vamp}}. Due to the stat being unused, this property is likewise deprecated. * '''EnableCallForHelp:''' When enabled, the damage instance triggers enemy [[minion]] aggression on the user. * '''EnableKill:''' When disabled, the damage instance will never be able to deal lethal damage. Mostly used for systems other than champion and minion combat. * '''RespectDodge:''' When enabled, the damage instance will be prevented via {{tip|dodge}} effects (e.g. {{cai|Jubilant Veil|Nilah}}, {{cai|Counter Strike|Jax}}). * '''RespectImmunity:''' When disabled, the damage instance will ignore all death protection effects and [[kill]] the enemy. {{tip|Spell shield}} may still prevent the application of the effect, if applicable. * '''TriggerDamageEvents:''' When disabled, the damage instance will ignore effects that trigger from the damage type and will behave as it were not considered one (except for stat tracking). * '''TriggerOnHitEvents:''' When enabled, the damage instance will apply {{tip|on-hit|on-hit effects}}. === Unexpected effect tags === These effects have certain tags or combine properties of multiple tags in a manner that renders their behavior unexpected or complicated to players. Note that these are not necessarily considered bugs, however. * Only tagged '''AOE''' ({{cais|W|Malphite}} cone) * '''Proc''' damage that is also '''ActiveSpell''' ({{ri|Aftershock}}) * '''Item''' damage that is also '''BasicAttack''' ({{ii|Heartsteel}}, {{ii|Kraken Slayer}}) * '''Proc''' damage that is also '''AOE''' ({{cai|Infernum|Aphelios}} cone damage, {{cai|I|Galio}}, {{cai|W|Sivir}}) * '''Proc''' damage not tagged '''AOE''' ({{bi|Hextech Dragon Soul}}, {{cais|Q|Jinx}} Fishbones explosion, {{cai|I|Nocturne}}, {{cai|Q|Rek'Sai}} area attack, {{cais|The Relentless Storm|Volibear}} chain lightning, {{cais|Lightning Crash|Zeri}} chain lightning, {{ii|Luden's Echo}}) * Non-'''AOE''' damage that actually affects multiple enemies passively ({{cai|Sentry|Aphelios}} {{ai|Infernum|Aphelios}}, {{cai|W|Shaco}}) * Always '''AOE''' damage that actually potentially affects only a single target ({{cai|Binding Eclipse|Aphelios}}, {{cai|Q|Kai'Sa}}, {{cai|R|Katarina}}, {{cai|R|Lee Sin}}, {{cai|Q|Senna}} against minions, {{cai|Q|Sona}}, {{cai|W|Twisted Fate|Red Card}}, {{cai|E|Wukong}}, {{ii|Titanic Hydra}} target and cone.) * [[DoT]] effects not tagged '''Periodic''' ({{cai|I|Darius}}, {{bi|Aspect of the Dragon}}). * Repeating effects not tagged '''Periodic''' ({{cai|W|Ahri}}, {{cai|R|Akshan}}, {{cai|E|Bel'Veth}}, {{cai|R|Gangplank}}, {{cai|Q|Gwen}}, {{cai|W|Heimerdinger}}, {{cai|Pocket Pistol|Kled}}, {{cai|Q|Master Yi}} secondary hits, {{cai|E|Nunu}}, {{cai|W|Ornn}}, {{cai|E|Smolder}}, {{cai|Q|Swain}}, {{cai|R|Syndra}}, {{cai|R|Warwick}}, {{cai|Q|Zeri}}). ** Similar effects tagged '''Periodic''' ({{cai|Q|Kai'Sa}} additional hits, {{cai|R|Lucian}}, {{cai|Q|Taliyah}} additional hits, {{cai|R|Katarina}}) * '''Pet''' basic attacks tagged '''BasicAttack''' ({{cis|Annie}} {{ui|Tibbers}}, {{cis|Ivern}} {{ui|Daisy}}, {{cis|Malzahar}} {{ui|Voidling}} and {{cis|Yorick}} {{ui|Maiden of the Mist}}) - can trigger {{bi|Infernal Dragon Soul}} and be reduced by {{ii|Plated Steelcaps}}, but cannot apply {{ri|Conqueror}} * '''Pet''' basic attacks ''not'' tagged '''BasicAttack''' ({{cai|I|Elise|Spiderling}}, {{cai|Q|Heimerdinger}}, {{cai|W|Shaco}}, {{cai|I|Yorick|Mist Walker}}, {{cai|I|Zyra}}) - cannot trigger {{bi|Infernal Dragon Soul}} nor be reduced by {{ii|Plated Steelcaps}}, but can apply {{ri|Conqueror}} * Ability-modified attacks that are not tagged '''BasicAttack''' ({{cai|W|Twisted Fate}}) {{bug|2|V13.5 patch notes: 'when you bonk someone with a staff it really will be protected by Steelcaps' / “An Auto’s an Auto, No Matter the Code”}} * Attack '''additional''' damage that applies lifesteal but is not tagged '''BasicAttack''' ({{cai|I|Riven}}, {{cai|Q|Vayne}}, {{cai|Q|Wukong}}, {{cai|I|Xin Zhao}}) ** Similar effects that apply lifesteal and are tagged '''BasicAttack''' ({{cai|W|Kled}}, {{cai|Q|Rengar}} and {{ai|R|Rengar}}) == Damage values == === Base values and character statistics ratios === === 0 Damage Instances === The following effects deal 0 {{tip|proc damage|nolink=true}}, triggering events that occur upon dealing/taking damage (such as drawing turret aggro and the [[combat|in-combat]] status), but not applying spell effects. * {{cai|Crystallize|Anivia}} * {{cai|Tempered Fate|Bard}} * {{cai|Essence Flux|Ezreal}} (on application) * {{cai|Explosive Charge|Tristana}} (on application) * {{cai|Pillar of Ice|Trundle}} * {{cai|Dark Procession|Yorick}} * {{cai|Time Bomb|Zilean}} (when it snaps onto an enemy) * {{si|Ignite}} (on application) The following abilities deal 0 {{tip|ability damage|nolink=true}}, triggering events that occur upon dealing/taking damage (such as drawing turret aggro and the combat status), while also applying spell effects. * {{cai|Sanguine Pool|Vladimir}} (final tick) {{ci|Neeko}} can deal 0 damage with certain {{ai|Inherent Glamour|Neeko|disguises}}. === Critical strike === A damage instance can '''[[critical strike|critically strike]]''' when it is implemented as such on an active attack or ability. Damage that critically strikes has been modified by a percentage above 100%, thus deals increased damage. Most critical strikes interact exclusively with {{stil|{{as|critical strike chance}}}}, {{stil|{{as|critical strike damage}}}}, and {{iis|Randuin's Omen}} {{nie|Resilience}}. The highest critical strike damage instance is also tracked in the post-game statistics.

Most on-hit effects, and spells will be unaffected, unless specified otherwise (e.g. {{cai|Runic Blade|Riven}}). By default, {{stil|{{as|critical strike chance}}}} above 100% does nothing. 1)} \Bigr) = 1.6000 average damage per attack (1.6000x average damage multipler) || 2 Crit Items, With Infinity Edge |} ;Average damage explanation Intuitively understand that critical strikes can be considered a 'percent chance' to increase damage by 'some percent' (with variance of course) along with some math to convert it to a multiplier
Crit multiplier explanation
* For a 175% (1.75x) crit multiplier, this 'some percent' damage increase is 75% (Add 0.75x base damage)
* For a 200% (2.00x) crit multiplier, this 'some percent' damage increase is 100% (Add 1.00x base damage)
* For a 230% (2.30x) crit multiplier, this 'some percent' damage increase is 130% (Add 1.30x base damage)
* For a CritMod (?.??x) crit multiplier, this 'some percent' damage increase is (CritMod% - 100%) (Add [CritMod - 1.00]x base damage) Some abilities or characters have a crit multiplier attached to them also. (e.g {{cai|Way of the Wanderer|Yasuo}}) Simply multiply by that number to get the final result.
Crit chance explanation
With a 25% 'percent chance' to increase damage by 'some percent', this is equivalent to (on average, with some variance) increasing your damage dealt by 25% of your 'some percent' damage increase. * A 25% 'percent chance' to increase damage by 75% is equivalent to increasing your damage by 18.75% (25% of a +75% damage increase is a 1.1875x damage increase)
* A 1% 'percent chance' to increase damage by 75% is equivalent to increasing your damage by 0.75% (1% of a +75% damage increase is a 1.0075x damage increase)
* A 25% 'percent chance' to increase damage by 100% is equivalent to increasing your damage by 25% (25% of a +100% damage increase is a 1.25x increase)
* A 1% 'percent chance' to increase damage by 100% is equivalent to increasing your damage by 1% (1% of a +100% damage increase is a 1.01x increase)

[[Armor]] and [[Magic Resistance]]'' === Calculating applied damage === ''See also: [[Shields]]'' ==Subtypes== ===Resistance subtypes=== ''See also: [[Armor]] and [[Magic Resistance]]'' Resistance subtypes are a secondary typing system that exists to promote [[champion classes]] by diversifying the effectiveness of items and champion match-ups. There is a small selection of effects that are triggered by specific subtypes rather than the above archetypes - e.g. {{ii|Morellonomicon}} will trigger on anything with the {{as|magic damage}} subtype, including abilities, basic attacks and on-hit effects (i.e. {{ii|Wit's End}} will trigger Morellonomicon on a champion with no other source of magic damage). These are the damage types visible to players in-game. {| class="article-table" !Name!!Description!!Example |- |{{tip|Physical damage}}||A damage type thematically associated with making physical contact, such as fists, swords and the physical projectiles of bows and guns. {{sti|Armor}} reduces incoming physical damage.||Most basic attacks; most {{as|AD-scaling}} abilities; some item effects. |- |{{tip|Magic damage}}||A damage type thematically associated with non-physical, such as magic or the supernatural. {{sti|Magic resistance}} reduces incoming magic damage.||Most {{as|AP-scaling}} abilities; some item effects. |- |{{tip|True damage}}||A damage type thematically associated with bypassing the target's defenses. Not to be confused with {{tip|raw damage}}.||A select few sources, such as {{si|Smite}}, {{si|Ignite}}, {{ai|Silver Bolts|Vayne}} and {{ai|Reckless Swing|Olaf}}. |} ==Calculating Damage== : ''Also see: [[Damage modifier]]. The following effects influence damage as non-zero values, in no particular order of calculation. They may originate from the attacker or the target. * Percentage damage amplification * Percentage damage reduction * Flat damage reduction * Resistances, meaning {{stil|armor}} and {{stil|magic resistance}}, against {{as|physical damage}} and {{as|magic damage}}, respectively * Resistances reduction * Resistances penetration, meaning {{stil|armor penetration}} and {{stil|magic penetration}} Resistances effectively reduce the respective damage subtype (physical or magic) by a '''percentage'''. However, '''"percent damage reduction"''' is a different, independent effect: abilities such as {{cai|Unbreakable Will|Alistar}} and item effects such as {{iis|Plated Steelcaps}} ''Plating'' may grant it as a beneficial effect while effects such as {{si|Exhaust}} may apply it as a [[debuff]]. Percent damage modifiers {{tip|stacks multiplicatively|stack multiplicatively}} with the damage reduction achieved through resistances. After the physical and magic damage is affected by the various reductions, it is applied to the target in {{stil|health|health amount}}. This amount received by the target is called ''post-mitigation damage''. ==Capped Damage== Some abilities, scaling with {{as|target's health}}, have a capped amount of damage they can deal to a target. This is made to avoid dealing massive damage to targets with a lot of health, most often against only {{tip|minions}} and/or {{tip|monsters}}. *If the ability deals enough damage (before damage reductions) to reach the cap, the ability's damage is reduced to the cap and damage reductions are then applied. This means that against a target that has negative armor or magic resistance the ability's post-mitigation damage can be higher than the cap. ==Misconceptions== The resistance types—physical, magic and true—are often regarded by players to be the archetypal damage types, which leads to a lot of misconceptions. For example, some players believe that magic damage, ability damage and AP are all interchangeable terms, with even prominent streamers referring to abilities as dealing "AP damage" and "AD damage". This is incorrect. It is possible for basic attacks to deal magic damage (e.g. {{ci|Thresh}} with a point in {{Ai|Flay|Thresh}}); it is possible for abilities to deal physical damage (e.g. {{ci|Riven}}); it is possible for AD-scaling abilities to deal magic damage (e.g. {{ci|Shyvana}}); and it is possible for non-magic damage to apply spell effects (e.g. {{ii|Luden's Echo}} would trigger on Riven if she chose to buy it, although she's discouraged due to her having no AP scalings). Similarly, many players believe that life steal and spell vamp are specific to physical and magic damage, respectively. Life steal will apply to anything classified as basic damage (including the magic damage from {{ai|Takedown|Nidalee}} and {{ai|Infinite Duress|Warwick}} and true damage from {{ai|Hextech Munitions|Corki}}), and spell vamp will apply to anything classified as ability damage (including the physical damage from {{ai|Comet Spear|Pantheon}} and true damage from {{ai|Reckless Swing|Olaf}}). ==See also== *[[Damage modifier]] *[[Magic damage]] *[[Physical damage]] *[[True damage]] {{Gameplay elements}} [[de:Schaden]] [[es:Daño]] [[pl:Obrażenia]] [[ru:Урон]] [[zh:伤害]] [[Category:Gameplay elements]]
